title: Calisthenics — Advanced Skills
subtitle: Handstand and L-sit skill work for an established athlete
coaching_note: Skill work needs a fresh nervous system — do this before any heavy strength session, not after. Quality attempts beat volume here; stop a block if your form is falling apart from fatigue, not just when the timer runs out.

exercises.name: Wrist Prep (circles, stretches, weight shifts)
exercises.form_cue: Full range circles, then rock your weight forward and back on flat hands on the floor.
exercises.why: Wrists absorb heavy load in both handstand and parallette work — never skip this.

exercises.name: Band Overhead Pass-Through
exercises.form_cue: Wide grip, arms straight, move slow through the full arc overhead and back.
exercises.why: Opens the shoulder flexion range a handstand demands.

exercises.name: Wall Walks
exercises.form_cue: Hands shoulder-width, walk your feet up the wall until arms are vertical. Squeeze core and glutes at the top, walk back down slow.
exercises.why: Builds the shoulder strength and stacked alignment a freestanding handstand needs.

exercises.name: Freestanding Handstand Attempts
exercises.form_cue: Kick up with control, find the balance point through your fingertips, not your wrist. Bail early and often — that's how you build the instinct.
exercises.why: The freestanding hold is the actual skill — everything else in this block builds toward this specific practice.

exercises.name: Handstand Push-up (wall, pike or full)
exercises.form_cue: Head lowers to just above the floor between your hands, press back to full lockout. Use a wall for balance if freestanding isn't there yet.
exercises.why: Adds strength on top of the hold — once the hold is solid, this is the next natural progression.

exercises.name: Full L-Sit Hold (parallettes)
exercises.form_cue: Arms locked straight on the parallettes, legs fully extended and parallel to the floor. Push your shoulders down away from your ears.
exercises.why: The core and hip flexor strength built here transfers directly into handstand alignment and most other advanced skills.

exercises.name: V-Sit Attempts
exercises.form_cue: From the L-sit, raise your legs above hip height toward a V shape. Small controlled attempts, not a grind to failure.
exercises.why: The next step past L-sit — only attempt once 10s L-sit holds feel genuinely solid.

exercises.name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Arm straight, palm up, gently pull your fingers back with the other hand.
exercises.why: Handstand and parallette work load the wrist hard — release it before you're done.

exercises.name: Foam Roll: Lats and Shoulders
exercises.form_cue: Slow passes, pause on tight spots for a few seconds.
exercises.why: Releases the shoulder tension from all the pressing and holding work.

progression_notes: Add 3-5s to freestanding handstand holds once bailing becomes rare. Move from wall handstand push-ups to freestanding once holds pass 30s consistently. Add 2s to L-sit holds each week, attempt V-sit once 15s L-sit is solid.
